neighbours.label: first-person words of love, guilt or forgiveness quoted in advice about grief and caregiving ('I love you', 'Did I cause this?'), as against quoted everyday first-person speech in the same advice
fire: In the last days, many people simply tell their mother 'I love you' again.
After the funeral, a child may ask, 'Did I make Grandpa die?'
Hospice nurses encourage families to say 'I forgive you' while there is time.
Siblings sometimes whisper, 'Was it my fault that she got sick?'
Before the surgery, the old man said 'I love you' to each grandchild.
Counsellors hear grieving teens ask, 'Could I have stopped it?'
At his bedside she finally said, 'I'm sorry, and I love you.'
Young children often believe, 'I caused the divorce because I was bad.'
quiet: In the last days, many people simply tell their mother 'I brought soup' again.
After the funeral, a child may ask, 'Can I have some juice?'
Hospice nurses encourage families to say 'I parked outside' when they arrive.
Siblings sometimes whisper, 'Is it time for dinner yet?'
Before the surgery, the old man said 'I need my glasses' to each nurse.
Counsellors hear grieving teens ask, 'Can I leave early today?'
At his bedside she finally said, 'I'll open the window now.'
Young children often say, 'I want the blue cup, not the red one.'
